chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about mining operations for various ores in specific geographic locations, including details on the largest operation, its location, access routes, and ownership history.
chunks.page_content: The Kemess Mine is 400 km by road from Prince George. The Kemess Mine was originally owned by Royal Oak Mines. The Kemess Mine is located in the valley of Kemess Creek. Several mining operations for ores containing copper, lead, zinc and silver have occurred around Thutade Lake. The Kemess Mine is accessed by other resource routes. The largest mining operation around Thutade Lake is the Kemess Mine. The Kemess Mine is an iron and copper property. The Kemess Mine is now owned by Northgate Minerals. The Kemess Mine is accessed by the Omineca Resource Road.

chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the operational history and ownership changes of the Kemess Mine from 1998 to 2014.
chunks.page_content: Northgate Minerals bought the Kemess Mine in 1999. Northgate Minerals was taken over by AuRico Gold in 2011. In 2014, AuRico Gold partitioned off its portion of Kemess Mine ownership. The Kemess Mine closed in 2011. Northgate Minerals operated the Kemess Mine until its closure in 2011. The Kemess Mine was operated by Royal Oak Mines from 1998 to 1999. AuRico Gold created a new company called AuRico Metals in 2014.

chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the ownership, location, operational timeline, financial performance, and environmental legacy of the Colomac Mine.
chunks.page_content: The Federal Government of Canada became owners of the Colomac Mine. The Colomac Mine reopened in 1994 under Royal Oak Mines Inc. The Federal Government of Canada became owners of the environmental issues related to the Colomac Mine. The Colomac Mine was operated by Neptune Resources Limited. The cleanup effort for the Colomac Mine might be too late at this stage. The Colomac Mine operated between 1994 and 1997. A major cleanup effort is under way to prevent the Colomac Mine from polluting the environment. Royal Oak Mines was forced into bankruptcy due to low gold prices and high cost of mining. Neptune Resources Limited had little success in making a profit during its operation of the Colomac Mine. The Colomac Mine operated between 1990 and 1992. The Colomac Mine was a privately owned and operated open pit gold mine. Public Works and Government services is the current contracting authority for the Colomac Mine. The Colomac Mine is now owned and controlled by the Indigenous and Northern Affairs department of the Federal government. The Colomac Mine was located 220 km northwest of Yellowknife in the Northwest Territories in Canada.
